habitat: Arboreal in broad-leaved woodland. Pairs when breeding, otherwise nomadic flocks of mostly one sex. Resident in the extreme northwest.
summary: A fairly common summer resident. The male's iridescent upperparts appear purple or coppery, and the underparts are white. The female has a yellow gape and yellow eyes, and lacks black ear-covert markings. The immature is like the female with darker eyes. The call is a short series of pleasant slurred notes. Newman does not name the months. The Kemp name Plumcoloured Starling and the code VB were left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common summer resident and also says it is resident in the extreme northwest. The months are not named, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. Purple or coppery is not stored as one upperpart colour. The female body colours are not given. The grade A call is from Senegal. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login tjeerd is credited. The Kemp name Plumcoloured Starling and the code VB were left unchanged.
